question: What changed in OpenCode 2.3.0 and when was it released?
report:
# OpenCode 2.3.0: Release Overview and Comprehensive Change Analysis

## Release Date and Version Context

OpenCode v2.3.0 was released on November 13, 2026, at 08:55 UTC, as published by the GitHub Actions automated release system with the commit hash `a6b15d3` ([GitHub Releases](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases)). The release is marked as immutable, meaning only the release title and notes can be modified after publication. This version represents a significant milestone in the OpenCode V2 series, following a rapid cadence of releases throughout late October and early November 2026, including v2.2.1 through v2.2.7 and the process-daemon sub-package updates (v0.5.0 on November 5 and v0.5.2 on November 11) ([GitHub Releases](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases)).

The v2.3.0 release is documented in the project's official CHANGELOG.md file, which lists it as "v2.3.0 — 2026-11-13" and positions it as the newest entry in the release notes for OpenCode V2 ([CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/CHANGELOG.md)). As of November 14, 2026, v2.3.0 was confirmed as the current stable version of the software ([Opencode Asia Changelog](https://www.opencode.asia/changelog/)).

## Primary Highlight: Background Subagents by Default

The single most significant change in OpenCode 2.3.0 is the fundamental redesign of how subagents operate. According to the release notes, "Subagents now return immediately, continue in the background, and report back whenever they become idle. You can keep working in the parent session while multiple subagents run concurrently" ([GitHub Releases](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases)). This change was implemented in pull request #63382, which was merged on November 11, 2026 ([Automater News](https://automater.ai/news/opencode-2-3-0-background-subagents-default/)).

### Technical Details of the Subagent Redesign

The change represents a complete architectural shift in how the subagent tool functions. Before v2.3.0, the default behavior was for a subagent call to block the parent session until the child completed its work, returning the answer inline. Parallel execution was opt-in via a `background: true` parameter. In v2.3.0, the foreground blocking path has been deleted entirely ([Automater News](https://automater.ai/news/opencode-2-3-0-background-subagents-default/)).

The behavioral change can be summarized as follows:

| Aspect | Before v2.3.0 | After v2.3.0 |
|--------|--------------|--------------|
| Default behavior | Block parent, return answer inline | Return session ID immediately, report on idle |
| Background mode | Opt-in via `background: true` | Always active, no flag available |
| Parent session | Blocked until child completes | Free to continue working |
| `jobs.block` parameter | Available | Removed |
| Ctrl+B handoff | Available for subagents | Removed |
| Inline answer | Default return format | No longer exists |

There is no configuration flag to revert to the previous behavior. The `background` option has been removed from the subagent tool entirely, and the `jobs.block` parameter has been deleted from the codebase ([Automater News](https://automater.ai/news/opencode-2-3-0-background-subagents-default/)). This makes it the biggest default behavior flip since OpenCode 2.0 introduced background subagents as an optional feature.

### Impact on Existing Workflows

This change is explicitly breaking for any automation or workflow that previously read a subagent's answer inline. Code that expected a synchronous return value from a subagent call will break upon upgrade ([Automater News](https://automater.ai/news/opencode-2-3-0-background-subagents-default/)). The new model requires developers to handle asynchronous reporting patterns, where the parent session receives notifications each time a child subagent transitions to an idle state.

## Additional Changes in v2.3.0

### TUI Transcript Verbosity

The Terminal User Interface (TUI) transcript verbosity now defaults to "low." In this mode, each run of tools and thoughts is summarized into a single collapsible activity row, reducing visual clutter during long sessions. If a user had previously configured a `session.verbosity` setting, that preference is preserved and not overridden by the new default ([Opencode Asia Changelog](https://www.opencode.asia/changelog/)).

### Desktop App: Jump to Message

The desktop application received a new "Jump to message" feature accessible through the command palette. Users can open it or use the keyboard shortcut Cmd+Alt+G (Ctrl+Alt+G on Windows and Linux) to search prompts across the current session and jump directly to a specific message, including prompts that have not yet been loaded into the visible timeline ([Opencode Asia Changelog](https://www.opencode.asia/changelog/)).

## Broader November 2026 Changes (v2.2.x through v2.3.0)

While v2.3.0 is the headline release, the November 2026 period encompassed numerous improvements across the OpenCode ecosystem that provide important context for the release cycle.

### Shell and Command Improvements

Shell results now end with an explicit "Exit code: N" line. Commands that are killed by a signal display the signal name, and timeout messages indicate how long the system waited and suggest increasing the timeout value ([Gradually Changelog](https://www.gradually.ai/en/changelogs/opencode/)). Additionally, when the `read` tool cannot find a file, it now suggests close matches based on different capitalization, alternative extensions, small typos, or the matching path within the project ([GitHub Releases](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases)).

### Prompt Cache Warming

A new intelligent cache warming system was introduced that times its pings based on the model's `cache.ttl` by default (using `interval: "auto"`), or every 4 minutes when no TTL is specified. Models whose cache lifetime exceeds the warming duration are no longer pinged, reducing unnecessary API calls ([Gradually Changelog](https://www.gradually.ai/en/changelogs/opencode/)). This was also documented as a core improvement with provider- and model-specific session warming settings ([CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/CHANGELOG.md)).

### MCP Server Improvements

Multiple improvements were made to Model Context Protocol (MCP) server handling:

- When MCP servers connect, disconnect, or change tools, Code Mode now sends the model a short list of what changed instead of the entire tool catalog ([Gradually Changelog](https://www.gradually.ai/en/changelogs/opencode/)).
- Remote MCP servers that rotate refresh tokens no longer log users out when the TUI, desktop app, background service, or several projects refresh the same login simultaneously ([Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/sst/opencode)).
- A temporary failure while refreshing an MCP OAuth token now preserves the login for the next attempt instead of marking the server as needing authentication ([Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/sst/opencode)).
- MCP tool calls no longer fail when the server's result does not match the tool's own output schema, preventing completed actions from being incorrectly reported as failed ([Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/sst/opencode)).
- Shared MCP connections were introduced through a `pool: true` option, allowing one connection to be shared across projects with the same setup, reducing process count and improving startup speed ([CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/CHANGELOG.md)).

### GitHub Copilot Integration Fixes

Several bug fixes were applied to the GitHub Copilot integration:

- Session costs now use the actual amount charged by Copilot rather than a catalog estimate, and content-filter errors now name the specific filter that blocked the response ([Gradually Changelog](https://www.gradually.ai/en/changelogs/opencode/)).
- GitHub Copilot now picks up a new API endpoint after a plan change on its next model refresh, eliminating the need to sign in again ([Gradually Changelog](https://www.gradually.ai/en/changelogs/opencode/)).

### SDK Improvements

The SDK received several enhancements during this period:

- `session.generate` now returns tokens and cost alongside text ([Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/sst/opencode)).
- `credential.updated` events now include the `integrationID` and `credentialID` of the login that changed ([Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/sst/opencode)).
- Predicate questions in `client.experimental.generate.decisions` now accept optional `criteria: { true?, false? }` parameters ([Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/sst/opencode)).

### Accessibility and UI Fixes

- Selects, menus, tooltips, and toasts opened from a dialog are now reachable by screen readers ([Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/sst/opencode)).
- Closing the last side panel tab now slides the panel shut ([Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/sst/opencode)).
- An error message appears when a path cannot be opened in its default application ([Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/sst/opencode)).
- Cut, Copy, Paste, and Select All in the right-click menu now follow the application language ([Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/sst/opencode)).
- Scrolling titlebar search results no longer jump back when late results arrive ([Releasebot](https://releasebot.io/updates/sst/opencode)).

### Experimental Features

An experimental bytecode VM for Code Mode was added, off by default, enabled via `experimental.codemode_vm: true` or the environment variable `OPENCODE_FLAGS=codemode_vm` ([CHANGELOG.md](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/CHANGELOG.md)).

## Process-Daemon Sub-Package Updates

The `@opencode/pty` package (process-daemon) received its own version updates during this period. Version 0.5.0 was released on November 5, 2026, and version 0.5.2 was released on November 11, 2026, both using protocol version 8 ([GitHub Releases](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases)). These releases were signed with GitHub's verified GPG key (ID: B5690EEEBB952194) and published to npm.

## Context: Preceding Releases Leading to v2.3.0

Understanding v2.3.0 requires awareness of the rapid release cadence that preceded it:

| Version | Release Date | Key Feature |
|---------|-------------|-------------|
| v2.2.1 | Oct 29, 2026 | `/goal` command, image generation, new model picker |
| v2.2.2 | Oct 29, 2026 | Image generation by default, faster worktree selection |
| v2.2.3 | Oct 30, 2026 | Claude Agent provider, faster long sessions |
| v2.2.4 | Oct 30, 2026 | Persistent desktop terminals, interactive artifacts |
| v2.2.5 | Oct 30, 2026 | (Additional fixes) |
| v2.2.6 | Nov 6, 2026 | Shared MCP connections, GUI plugin themes, mobile composer dock |
| v2.2.7 | Nov 10, 2026 | (Additional improvements) |
| v2.3.0 | Nov 13, 2026 | Background subagents by default |

This rapid cadence—seven patch/minor releases in approximately two weeks—demonstrates the project's aggressive development pace ([GitHub Releases](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/releases)).

## Assessment and Significance

The v2.3.0 release represents a philosophical shift in OpenCode's approach to parallelism. By making background subagents the only mode, the project signals that concurrent execution is not an advanced feature but a fundamental expectation. The removal of the foreground path eliminates a class of user confusion around blocking behavior and forces all workflows to adopt the asynchronous pattern. While this is a breaking change for existing automation, it simplifies the mental model: subagents are always background tasks that report back when idle ([Automater News](https://automater.ai/news/opencode-2-3-0-background-subagents-default/)).

The combination of the subagent redesign, reduced TUI verbosity, and the desktop jump-to-message feature collectively addresses the challenge of managing long, complex sessions with multiple concurrent operations—a growing concern as AI coding agents handle increasingly sophisticated multi-step workflows.
